column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.4.3 = v720896). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, NintendoWare G3d2 / Ui2d / Vfx2, Havok), SDK 20.5.22, NVN; modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie) + sdk.
# subsdk0 and sdk are the same builds as Breath of the Wild 1.9.0's. Most RomFS files are zstd with dictionaries (*.zs; the dictionaries are Pack/ZsDic.pack.zs).
# Shaders: Shader/*.bfsha.zs (BNSH; material.bfsha holds most) and the layout shaders in Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_NX_NVN.release.sarc.zs.
# main imports nn::ro (loads NRO modules at run time). Values marked "Breath of the Wild's" are not measured for this game yet

column1: # the virtual gamepad starts in the 3D layout (D-pad, right stick, L3 / R3): the right stick turns the camera
# The NPDM declares 24 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true and the game's memory lives in the alias region (as Engage's, see 0100A6301214E000/game.tsv).
# The game also calls SetHeapSize(0x86000000) in nninitStartup (2.1 GB of the pool as its heap; a 2 GB heap region aborts there with 0xd401).
# What it can map is bounded by the pool less the heap (1.1 GB). The sdk build's node area is cut from ~1 GB to 62 MB (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py): measured on the Mac, the alias region is then used

# up to +1.75 GB on the Great Sky Island with 1.0 GB mapped. Without the cut it reached +2.25 GB at the first descent and the game took a memory shortage (MSF, a Blood Moon that puts Link back, issue #70).

# So 5 GB, the total proven on a phone (one reservation of at most 6 GB without the extended virtual addressing entitlement): 256 MB in front + 2.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 2.125 GB heap region
# Streamed textures are written by the CPU straight into pool memory (already in GPU layout) and published with nvnMemoryPoolFlushMappedRange (hle_nvn.c ft_add)
# Ultrawide's camera (patches.py camera_aspect, nvn_mtl.m aspect_ui): the vertex shaders that draw the HUD and menus onto the game's floating-point final picture (their keys'
# first 8 hex digits, which also take their translated variants). Their quads are squeezed to the middle of the picture, so the HUD keeps its shape once Stretch widens it;
# the inventory's scene pictures and full-screen triangles are not. From ComicBit/nxnative 76f085084 (MIT), which took them from MacNativeGames' nvn_mtl.m (MIT; notice in nvn_aspect.h)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host decides each frame's step in whole vsyncs and holds the frame that long (rewriter stubs at FPSLocker's sites, patches.py FRAME_STEP);
# 30 when 60 does not hold, game time = real time. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) saves power, 0 = the game's own step. Until the host has decided a step
# (the first frames) the stub steps by the measured frame time
# The GPU clock kick and the present repeat, as Donkey Kong Bananza's, Mario Kart World's and Star Fox's (hle_nvn.c clock_kick_tick, nvn_present_repeat.inc): this game's
# iPhone run (bd454996, 23 min) showed the same stuck clock (the GPU probe at 3.2x, held at 30 or lower in stretches; a swipe to the Home Screen and back brought 60 back at once),
# and its old clock rescue fired 8 times without lifting it, so the kick turns that rescue off (NX18-X2.0 gpu-clock-collapse.md). DM_CLOCK_KICK=0 / DM_PRESENT_REPEAT=0 turn them off
# The GPU headroom controller through the live render scale (nvn_drs_gpu.h, hle_nvn.c drs_gpu_tick): while the GPU time per frame stays over 75% of the target's frame time the
# host lowers the 3D views' factor at state +0x14 one step (0.9 to 0.5 of the side; at Render scale 1.0 the stubs take the lower of it and the game's own dynamic scale), and
# takes each step back when the GPU time per frame did not fall. Off since 2026-11-23: on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (Tears of the Kingdom, c8351b8cf, about 7 min) the factor
# held 0.5-0.6 for about 5 min with the GPU time per frame unchanged (10-11 ms, as at 1.0) and no softer picture seen, so +0x14 does not reach the views' size on the
# device; Breath of the Wild's lever is unmeasured. On again once a run shows the factor cutting the GPU time
